disease_label_per_paper: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by shock and multiple organ dysfunction in a 5-year-old girl
presentation_summary: 5-year-old girl with developmental delay, returned from the Democratic Republic of the Congo 2 weeks earlier without malaria chemoprophylaxis, presented with 5 days of fever, progressive fatigue, vomiting, diarrhea, and reduced oral intake.

Outside hospital: tachycardic, tachypneic, lethargic, clinically dehydrated, diffuse abdominal tenderness. WBC 17,400/uL, Hb 8.8 g/dL, platelets 4,500/uL, BUN 76 mg/dL, creatinine 1.89 mg/dL, K 5.9 mmol/L, total bilirubin 6.9 mg/dL, AST 189 U/L, ALT 99 U/L, lactate 8 mmol/L.
On transfer to the tertiary emergency department (same day): altered mental status, cool extremities, fever 103.5 F, tachycardia with age-appropriate blood pressure; head CT without cerebral edema.
time_zero_definition: Outside-hospital presentation and same-day transfer to the tertiary emergency department (before antimalarial therapy); fever onset 5 days earlier.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Later course: intubation, cardiac arrest, parasitemia 19% on HD2, peak lactate 21.9 mmol/L, secondary TMA (ADAMTS13 22.6%, sC5b-9 693 ng/mL), CRP 26.4 mg/dL, ferritin 20,877 ng/mL, IL-6 239 pg/mL, sIL-2R 5,296 U/mL, bilirubin peak 29.1 mg/dL
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: she progressed to refractory shock with multiple organ failure, with a peak lactate of 21.9 mmol/L and parasitemia rising to 19% on HD 2 ... Inflammatory profiling revealed marked hyperinflammatory phenotype: C-reactive protein (26.4 mg/dL), ferritin (20,877 ng/mL) ...
She was admitted to the PICU for severe P. falciparum malaria complicated by shock and evolving multiple organ dysfunction

actual_treatment: IV crystalloids and ceftriaxone at outside hospital; later cefepime and vancomycin
enteral artemether-lumefantrine bridging, IV artesunate (8 doses), atovaquone-proguanil
CRRT with selective cytopheretic device, then intermittent hemodialysis
fresh frozen plasma and therapeutic plasmapheresis for secondary TMA

outcome.source_text_value: she completed inpatient rehabilitation and was discharged home (HD 48) ... At follow-up, organ dysfunctions had resolved

quality_warnings: Heart rate, respiratory rate and blood pressure reported only qualitatively (tachycardic, tachypneic, age-appropriate BP).
Smear parasitemia/species identification is diagnosis-establishing and kept non-ranking.
Tertiary-ED repeat labs showing 'hemolysis and systemic inflammation' are unquantified and kept record-only.
Post-presentation deterioration, TMA work-up and cytokine profile belong to the hospital course and are not ranked.
